surface: Newton direction sign convention for maximization
source_issue: The source identifies B k with the Hessian in the general ascent framework, although that framework uses p equal to B inverse times the gradient; for maximization the Newton direction is minus the inverse Hessian times the gradient and therefore B k must be minus the Hessian.
target_action: Set B k equal to minus H at x k, stated p k equal to minus H inverse times the gradient, and distinguished pure unit-step Newton from variable-step Newton.

source_issue: The reader splits its algorithm across two Maple listings whose component rights are unclear or external and which can loop or accept a non-ascent Newton direction without an explicit failure contract.
target_action: Excluded both Maple components and supplied independently authored two-part locale-neutral pseudocode with Hessian solve, ascent test, line-search contract, gradient stopping rule, iteration bound, path return, and explicit failure states; no Maple syntax or implementation text was copied.

source_issue: The source uses a negative diagonal entry to discuss positive definiteness even though maximization requires negative definiteness, omits the Hessian inverse from the Newton direction, multiplies the direction by the line parameter inside its definition, and defines phi as a vector rather than f evaluated along a line.
target_action: Used the negative determinant to establish indefiniteness, computed the correct direction minus H inverse gradient, verified its directional derivative is about minus 1.212660274, defined phi of s as F at x zero plus s p N, identified the violated ascent-direction precondition, and required rejection or bounded failure instead of infinite shrinking or returning zero as a positive step.

source_issue: The source maximization subscript reads norm x minus one rather than norm x equals one and does not identify the underlying vector norm.
target_action: Defined the matrix norm as the maximum of norm M x over Euclidean unit vectors norm x equals one.

surface: Local pure-Newton convergence theorem and proof
source_issue: The source proof replaces submultiplicative norm inequalities by equalities, duplicates an equality, does not make the local ball invariant, does not separate finite termination from asymptotic convergence, and calls a quadratic upper estimate order at least two without establishing an exact positive asymptotic ratio.
target_action: Used continuity of the inverse Hessian on a compact ball, the integral mean-value identity, submultiplicativity and the integral norm inequality, a local Hessian modulus to choose an invariant contraction ball, and a Lipschitz-Hessian estimate LM over two times squared error; separated finite termination from Q-superlinear nonzero-error convergence and described the quadratic estimate as an upper bound rather than an exact order claim.

surface: Gradient-Newton hybrid attribution, example endpoint, and convergence exercises
source_issue: The source inconsistently attributes the same hybrid to Cauchy and Gauss, prints the nonstationary point one comma one as the limit even though the positive-y global maximizer is zero comma one, and asks for unconditional gradient-related and superlinear conclusions without uniform scaling, line-search, convergence, or negative-definite-limit hypotheses.
target_action: Used the neutral name gradient-Newton hybrid, disclosed the conflicting source attribution without choosing one, corrected the endpoint to zero comma one, required the Hessian test at each iteration, and added the compactness, uniform spectral, Armijo, convergent-iterate, negative-definite-limit, and finite-termination-alternative assumptions needed by the exercises.

surface: Modified Cholesky factorization and executable surface
source_issue: The excluded Maple listing places mu two directly on the factor diagonal rather than correcting the Schur pivot before taking a square root, never reports failure, and the prose claims unconditional closeness to the input from positive definiteness alone.
target_action: Replaced it with independently authored symmetric Schur-update pseudocode that keeps a pivot at least mu one or replaces it by mu two before square rooting, returns L and B equal to L L transpose plus corrected-pivot evidence, proves B positive definite from the positive diagonal, and makes closeness explicitly threshold dependent.

source_issue: The source uses a bold vector f for a scalar objective and leaves the approximation symbol between minus H and L L transpose without naming the actual positive-definite surrogate or the equality case.
target_action: Defined B k equal to L L transpose, used minus H approximately B k with equality exactly when no pivot is corrected, retained p equal to B inverse gradient, and stated the forward and backward triangular solves without forming an inverse.

source_issue: The prose says the factorization is applied to minus the Hessian but the printed factor uses the Hessian signs, sets both factor diagonals to one despite a safe first pivot, and consequently gives inconsistent z, p, and directional-product values.
target_action: Applied the disclosed pivot rule to A equal to minus H with mu one 0.1 and mu two 1, retained the safe first pivot, corrected only the negative second Schur pivot, solved both triangular systems exactly, and obtained gradient transpose p equal to 9 alpha over 10 plus 6241 alpha squared over 400, about 10.164315323 and positive.

source_issue: The reader splits the method across excluded Maple files, one of which uses an uninitialized iteration counter and hard-coded factorization thresholds, while neither surface exposes complete failure behavior.
target_action: Excluded both Maple files and supplied independent two-part pseudocode with explicit thresholds, iteration bound, gradient test, destructured factorization outputs for negative H, triangular solves, ascent check, Armijo backtracking, state update, returned path, and failure reports.

surface: Stationarity theorem for corrected Newton directions
source_issue: Pointwise positive definiteness of each inverse surrogate does not by itself make the direction sequence gradient related, and twice continuous differentiability plus fixed thresholds does not guarantee the whole iterate sequence converges.
target_action: Required uniform spectral bounds on every surrogate, fixed-parameter Armijo backtracking, and convergence of the iterate sequence; used those bounds to prove bounded directions and a uniform positive directional-product lower bound before applying the corrected Chapter 4 stationarity theorem.

surface: Eventual unmodified Newton behavior and superlinear convergence
source_issue: The source compares the threshold with pivots obtained from H rather than minus H, invokes continuity of f instead of continuity of the Hessian and Cholesky pivots, does not state all Armijo parameter or convergence hypotheses for the fixed and gradient-scaled thresholds, and does not separate finite termination from asymptotic superlinear convergence.
target_action: Chose mu one below the smallest Schur pivot of the ordinary Cholesky factorization of minus H at the negative-definite limit, used Hessian and pivot continuity to show corrections eventually cease, imposed zero less than sigma one less than one half and unit initial step, separated finite termination from Q-superlinear convergence, and made the dynamic-threshold exercise conditional on convergence to a negative-definite stationary point.
